statements.label: supported
statements.text: Recombined V H promoters make long, strong antisense RNAs across the upstream L1s, which pulls in the HUSH complex and AID.
statements.evidence: Recombined V H promoters generate long, strong antisense RNAs encoding upstream L1s, triggering the human silencing hub (HUSH) complex and AID recruitment, which we term L1-driven SHM.
statements.note: This chain from antisense transcription to HUSH and AID recruitment is what the abstract calls L1-driven SHM.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Inserting transcriptionally active L1s at non-immunoglobulin loci that normally lack upstream L1s produced off-target somatic hypermutation.
statements.evidence: Insertion of transcriptionally active L1s at non-immunoglobulin loci endogenously lacking upstream L1s promotes off-target SHM.
statements.note: The abstract reports off-target somatic hypermutation following insertion of active L1s at such loci.
